prompt: Why is f(g(x)) usually different from g(f(x))?
answer: Composition applies the machines in order: f(g(x)) feeds x to g first and g's output to f. Each machine changes its input in its own way, so changing which acts first changes what the second one sees. Squaring then adding 1 gives x^2 + 1; adding 1 then squaring gives (x + 1)^2, which differs by 2x.
